deviations: R1: FP8-pilot n-gram covers 0.64 < 0.8 of bf16 twin D programs; re-derived on bf16 twin programs (declared rule): [' if start']
T14: FP8-pilot n-gram covers 0.79 < 0.8 of bf16 twin D programs; re-derived on bf16 twin programs (declared rule): ['_counts']

HARDWARE: the pod has one RTX 4090 (24 GB), not the planned RTX A4500 (20 GB); bf16 Qwen3-8B fits, so no fallback (F1) was needed. vLLM runs with max_num_seqs=64 and max_num_batched_tokens=4096 instead of 32/2048 (scheduling only; the sampling distribution is unchanged).
NO C COMPILER on the machine: Triton/Inductor cannot build, so vLLM runs with enforce_eager=True and TORCH_COMPILE_DISABLE=1 (as in exp11); throughput only.

MODEL WEIGHTS live in the run's shared Hugging Face cache (HF_HUB_CACHE, Qwen/Qwen3-8B @ b968826d9c46dd6066d109eabc6255188de91218), not in a workspace hf_cache/ directory, following the run's storage rule that forbids re-pointing HF_HOME; nothing to delete in the workspace.

TWIN PADDING: ' .' fillers are appended to the end of the neutral segment (exp7's frozen implementation, src/prompts_v2.py: unpadded_segment + filler * d), which the plan's 'append fillers to N' wording is read as; every ban/twin pair has equal chat-formatted length and identical ids from the 'Task' token on (asserted).

GREEDY COVER operationalised (declared in the committed src/ngrams.py docstring before any veto sampling): each greedy step considers n-grams present in at least ceil(still-needed / slots-left) of the still-uncovered REF programs; with this pace rule 3 n-grams can always reach 0.8 when a cover exists.

HF TWIN CONTROL (1.7e) was run for every task (50 samples, same HF code path, no hook) instead of only when a random direction moved >= 20 attempts off D: a superset that removes the dependency on mid-process labels.

JUDGE: transient upstream HTTP 429 rate limits from gemini-2.5-flash-lite are retried with backoff (budget refusals never are); judge answers are cached by (judge model, task, sha256 of scrubbed code), and exp11's cache was reused (same judge, same prompt). Labels of identical programs (same task, same code sha256) are reused within the run.

VERDICT BRANCHES the plan leaves open are named explicitly in the committed code: C2b 'INCONCLUSIVE' (neither the confirm nor the disconfirm bar met, i.e. modal agreement without landing agreement); C1 'NO FAMILY ADVANCES' (no family advances and fewer than half of the gated events are unaimed). LADDER_EXISTS counts a shared modal label only when it is a survivor (not 'other').
HOOK TEST (c): the 1% displacement-norm tolerance is evaluated against the bf16 rounding bound of h0 + delta; measured max relative error 0.23% (all positions within 1%).

SCALE-UP: smoke runs (process A on T03+T05 with 2 samples per template; process B on T03 with 2 per direction) and then the full runs, instead of 10 -> 100 -> full; the full process A took ~6 min, B ~8 min, C ~4 min, so extrapolation was moot (results/timing.jsonl).

FRLP fp32 rescoring (S2b ii) covers the 50 cells of the 12 frozen tasks (the plan says 54: exp11 counted R2, which the freeze excluded). The scorer re-implements exp7s fp32-activation scorer (same numerics) rather than importing exp7 code, and passed the 5-program exp7 reproduction gate (max 0.021 nats).

POST-HOC (not pre-registered) analyses are kept separate in src/posthoc.py -> results/posthoc_sensitivity.json: defined-only wins, every family vs the uniform reference, the advance rule with UNIFORM as a competitor, and the closest ban-free arm to each ban landing.

POST-BAN PORTABILITY REVISION of the committed src/common.py: absolute input-artifact paths replaced by relative constants with environment-variable overrides (no logic, constant or seed changed). Appended to commitments.log as post_ban_revision (+ post_ban_note); the sealed bytes are preserved in audit/sealed_files/src_common.py.sealed (sha256 == committed hash) with the diff beside it; guard() verifies both. CPU re-analysis after the change is byte-identical.

Task: write a Python function solve(nums, k) that returns the k-th smallest value in nums. The argument nums is a list of integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 2000, and every value lies between -10000 and 10000 inclusive; values may repeat. The argument k is an integer with 1 <= k <= len(nums), counted from 1, so k = 1 asks for the minimum and k = len(nums) for the maximum. Repeated values are counted separately: for nums = [3, 1, 3] and k = 3 the answer is 3.
